questions.text: What is the primary user-experience benefit of streaming an LLM response as it is generated?

options.A: It guarantees that the complete answer requires fewer generated tokens.
options.B: It lets the user see initial content before the complete response is ready.
options.C: It removes the need to handle provider failures or output validation.
options.D: It guarantees that every model call finishes in less than one second.

questions.explanation: True incremental streaming reduces time until the user sees content, even when total generation time is unchanged.

questions.text: A provider outage causes many clients to retry simultaneously. Which recovery design reduces synchronized retries while bounding work?

options.A: Retry immediately forever and disable timeouts until the provider recovers.
options.B: Send all retries at fixed identical intervals with no attempt limit.
options.C: Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter, then an appropriate fallback.
options.D: Suppress failure logs and repeatedly resubmit the same request in a tight loop.

questions.explanation: Exponential backoff spreads retries over time, jitter reduces synchronization, and retry limits plus fallback bound recovery work.

questions.text: handle_streaming_request first awaits handle_request, which returns the complete response. It then collects every item from stream_response into a list before returning a dictionary. What does its caller receive?

options.A: Individual generated tokens immediately as the provider produces them.
options.B: An async generator that the caller can consume during the model call.
options.C: A response before generation finishes, followed by automatic SSE updates.
options.D: A final dictionary after generation and local word-by-word iteration finish.

questions.explanation: This method buffers the full response and consumes the local stream internally. It does not yield tokens to its caller or provide live provider streaming.
